# Cross-language golden vectors for the `VREC` recording container
# (one `key=hexbytes` per line).
#
# Generated from the Python reference implementation
# (python/visio_schema/mcap/crypto.py). Both python/tests/
# test_recording_crypto.py and cpp/tests/test_recording_crypto.cc load
# these bytes and assert THEIR implementation reproduces them.
#
# This is the fixture that matters most in the recording-encryption work.
# The device WRITES these bytes in C++ and the admin READS them in Python,
# and the two are separate implementations of one stream cipher. A drift
# between them does not fail loudly: it produces a card full of recordings
# that decrypt to convincing garbage, discovered long after the shift.
# Pinning both directions against committed bytes makes that a build
# failure instead.
#
# The key and nonce are deliberately recognisable counting patterns. They
# are TEST values; a real recording key is minted per client and never
# enters this repo.

vrec_key=000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f
vrec_nonce=404142434445464748494a4b
vrec_key_fp=630dcd2966c43366
# HMAC-SHA256(key, b'visio-rec-v1' + nonce) — the per-part key that
# actually runs the cipher, so one part's key reveals nothing about
# another's.
vrec_file_key=cf38b582f522f3b3d8651147b145086480aa604e1cc82e10db3589b559bad8e8
# The 32-byte plaintext header, exactly as written to the head of a part.
vrec_header=5652454301010000630dcd2966c43366404142434445464748494a4b00000000
# 200 bytes: crosses three ChaCha20 blocks and ends unaligned, so an
# off-by-one in block indexing or in the sub-block skip cannot pass.
vrec_
vrec_
